title: Platform systems & services playbook — dashboards, runbooks, roadmap (Q2 2026 addendum)
author: Ayesha Patel
body:
Overview
--------
This playbook consolidates canonical platform engineering guidance for the Platform Systems & Services area: system owners, dashboards and alerts standards, operational runbooks, recent retrospective findings, and the near-term roadmap (Q2 2026 addendum). It is intended for on-call engineers, platform owners, and SREs.

Scope
-----
- Services covered: platform-api, runtime-router, ingest-pipeline, queue-worker, batch-scheduler, metrics-ingest
- Observability stack: Prometheus (metrics), Alertmanager, Grafana (dashboards), Loki (logs), Tempo (traces)
- Audience: platform engineers, SRE, eng-platform product managers

Key contacts and ownership
-------------------------
- Platform systems lead: Marcus Chen (eng-platform)
- Observability owner: Rina Kapoor (eng-platform instrumentation)
- Pager rotation: platform-oncall@redwood.com (see team wiki for schedule)

Systems and services (summary table)
-----------------------------------
Service | Primary owner | SLO (success) | Latency SLO | Notes
platform-api | Marcus Chen | 99.95% successful requests (5m windows) | p95 < 250ms | Front door for REST SDK and webhooks
runtime-router | Diego Alvarez | 99.9% route success | p95 < 50ms routing hop | Routes requests to hosted/dedicated/private slots
ingest-pipeline | Priya Menon | 99.9% processing within 30s | n/a | Handles logs, metrics, telemetry
queue-worker | Jose Martinez | 99.5% jobs processed | job latency p95 < 60s | Backfill/backpressure tolerant
batch-scheduler | Operations team | 99% scheduled tasks | n/a | Nightly/long-running jobs
metrics-ingest | Rina Kapoor | 99.95% metric write success | n/a | Sharded Prometheus remote_write ingestion

Dashboards and alerts — standards
--------------------------------
Principles:
- Dashboards are for three audiences: on-call (live triage), owners (health trends), and capacity planning (long-term).
- Every production service must have a 1-page on-call dashboard that fits on a single 1920x1080 screen.
- Alerts must be actionable and cause a single, well-defined mitigation step. Use severity P1/P2/P3 mapping.

Required dashboard panels (on-call view):
1. Request rate (RPS) by route
2. Error rate (4xx/5xx) by code and endpoint
3. Latency (p50/p95/p99) timeseries
4. Instance count and autoscaler status
5. CPU, GPU (if applicable), memory, and queue depth
6. Recent logs sample (Loki quick query)
7. Traces: 90th percentile trace duration and top spans (Tempo)

Alerting thresholds (default templates)
- P1 (page immediately):
  - 5xx rate > 0.5% of requests for 5 continuous minutes OR
  - p95 latency > 1s for 5 continuous minutes OR
  - Total error budget burn rate > 5x for 1 hour
- P2 (investigate during working hours):
  - 5xx rate > 0.25% for 10 minutes OR
  - p95 latency > 600ms for 10 minutes OR
  - Autoscaler unable to scale (pods stuck Pending) for 10 minutes
- P3 (informational):
  - sustained increase in p50 latency by 20% over baseline for 24 hours
  - incremental increase in background job retry rate

Alert routing and escalation
- P1 -> platform oncall (pager duty) -> notify eng-platform leads -> create incident in Incident Tracker
- P2 -> slack #platform-ops and duty engineer -> owner notified by DM if unacknowledged for 30m
- P3 -> email to owners, no immediate paging

Prometheus/Alertmanager example (snippet)
- name: PlatformAPIHighError
  expr: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="platform-api",status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="platform-api"}[5m])) > 0.005
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: P1
  annotations:
    summary: "platform-api high 5xx rate"

Runbooks (canonical incident flow)
--------------------------------
1. Detection & triage
   - Check on-call dashboard and Alertmanager alert details. Note timestamps, affected regions, and request ids.
   - Run: grafana-query -> logs (Loki) -> traces (Tempo) to determine scope.
2. Initial mitigation (first 15 minutes)
   - If widespread 5xx: scale up platform-api (kubectl scale deployment/platform-api --replicas N+2) and enable temporary rate-limiting via runtime-router config to slow non-critical routes.
   - If single route: disable the route in runtime-router (set weight=0) and re-route to fallback model variant.
   - If job backpressure: pause new job enqueues by toggling queue-worker ingress flag (service flag: feature.queue_enqueue=false).
3. Stabilize & contain (15-60 minutes)
   - Open a private incident channel and assign roles: Incident Lead, Communications, Mitigation Engineer, Scribe.
   - Apply targeted rollback if a recent config or deploy is implicated: rollback platform-api to previous revision (kubectl rollout undo).
4. Recovery & verification
   - Wait for metrics to return to SLO for two consecutive 5-minute windows.
   - Run synthetic smoke tests (scripts/smoke/platform-api-smoke.sh) and verify affected customer flows.
5. Post-incident actions
   - Create postmortem within 72 hours with incident timeline, root cause, impact, and action items. Assign owners and due dates.

How-tos (common operational tasks)
--------------------------------
- Add a new on-call dashboard: Duplicate the template dashboard: Grafana -> Dashboards -> Manage -> Copy "platform-oncall-template" -> update datasource and queries -> save as "oncall-<service>" -> add to folder "Platform Oncall" and share with team.
- Add an alert rule: Create a new Prometheus rule under k8s/observability/rules/<service>-rules.yaml, lint with promtool, apply via CI. Example: kubectl apply -f <service>-rules.yaml --namespace=observability
- Run a controlled rollback: kubectl rollout undo deployment/<service> --to-revision=<rev> ; verify pods become Ready and p95 latency returns below SLO

Retrospective (Q1 2026 highlights & mitigations)
------------------------------------------------
What went well:
- SRE automation reduced mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) by 28% after alert deduplication work.
- New synthetic transactions detected two regressions prior to widespread customer impact.

What needs improvement:
- Several runbooks lacked specific rollback commands for the runtime-router; action: add explicit router rollback sections. (Owner: Diego Alvarez, due 2026-03-15)
- Dashboards had inconsistent panel naming across teams; action: enforce dashboard naming schema via CI lint (Owner: Rina Kapoor, due 2026-04-01)

Near-term roadmap (Q2 2026 addendum)
-----------------------------------
- Observability consolidation: migrate logs to Loki v3 and roll out trace-id correlation in Tempo (Q2 end).
- Synthetic transactions: expand coverage to dedicated/private deployment variants and surface pass/fail in on-call dashboards (Q2).
- SLO automation: implement automatic error budget burn alerts and scheduled review workflow (Q2- Q3).
- Dashboards as code: store dashboard JSON in git under infra/observability/dashboards and enable PR-based changes with Grafana CI (Q2).
- Playbook updates: add per-service router rollback steps and create playbook unit tests (synthetic verification) (Q2).

Operational runbook checklist (for owners)
----------------------------------------
- [ ] On-call dashboard exists and is up-to-date
- [ ] Alerts use standard templates and are actionable
- [ ] Runbook includes rollback + mitigation commands
- [ ] Synthetic smoke tests defined and runnable in CI
- [ ] Incident postmortem template ready in Confluence and linked

Appendix: useful commands and links
----------------------------------
- Grafana on-call dashboard template: https://grafana.internal.redwood.com/d/PLATFORM/oncall-template
- Prometheus rules repo: git@github.com:redwood/infra-observability.git//rules
- Smoke test script: repo infra/observability/scripts/smoke/platform-api-smoke.sh
- Common kubectl commands: kubectl -n platform rollout status deploy/platform-api ; kubectl -n platform logs -f deploy/platform-api

Notes
-----
This document is meant to be a living playbook; owners should update their service sections after every incident or quarterly review. See related pages for SLO definitions and the platform roadmap for cross-team dependencies.
